prompt: A bank's technology team has 5 compliance/tech projects competing for a fixed pool of 12 engineer-months this quarter. Recommend a prioritized sequence.
context: Projects (engineer-months required / regulatory deadline / business value): (1) AML transaction-monitoring rule update — 4 eng-months, hard regulatory deadline in 10 weeks, no direct revenue but avoids a known regulatory finding. (2) Core banking API modernization — 6 eng-months, no deadline, enables 3 other future initiatives. (3) Customer data deletion/right-to-erasure automation — 3 eng-months, regulatory deadline in 14 weeks. (4) Fraud-detection model retraining — 5 eng-months, no deadline, estimated to reduce fraud losses by $600K/year. (5) Internal reporting dashboard refresh — 2 eng-months, no deadline, convenience improvement only. Total capacity: 12 engineer-months.

binaryCriteria.description: Treats the two regulatory-deadline projects (AML rule update, data-deletion automation) as must-fund regardless of relative "business value", given the confirmed compliance exposure.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if either regulatory-deadline project is deferred or deprioritized below a non-deadline project.

binaryCriteria.description: The recommended set of funded projects sums to at or under the 12 engineer-month capacity constraint.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the recommended set requires materially more than 12 engineer-months without explicit descoping.

binaryCriteria.description: Allocates the ~5 eng-months remaining after the two mandatory projects to the fraud-model retraining (best value-per-cost fit) rather than the dashboard refresh or an initiative that does not fit.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the dashboard refresh is prioritized over fraud-model retraining with the remaining capacity.

goldNotes: A strong answer treats the two hard regulatory deadlines (AML rule update, 4 eng-months, 10-week deadline; data-deletion automation, 3 eng-months, 14-week deadline) as non-negotiable must-dos — together 7 eng-months — since missing them carries confirmed regulatory/compliance exposure, not just opportunity cost. With 5 eng-months of capacity remaining, it should prioritize fraud-model retraining ($600K/year value, 5 eng-months) over the dashboard refresh (2 eng-months, convenience-only) or the API modernization (6 eng-months — does not fit remaining capacity anyway). A weak answer ranks purely by "business value" and defers a hard-deadline regulatory item, or tries to fit all 5 projects (26 eng-months of work) into 12 eng-months of capacity without acknowledging the gap.
